title: Why the realised value sits above the decision interval's centre (daily_centre_v1)
request: The owner, 2026-10-26: find why the realised value sits a little above the interval's centre on known worlds (mean z +0.10 to +0.16), with a gate fixed before; keep the machine light.
spec: dclab_rnd/daily_centre_measure.py: 800 invented worlds an arm, the decision core alone; daily and share decisions with samples from the latest fold (as the engine) and from all rows (reported); per world the percentile midpoint, the samples' mean (dclab-core 0.120.1), z_mid and z_mean; per decision its own verdict: the bias by the interval of mean z_mid (established, closed inside 0.08, or inconclusive), the skew by mean (z_mid - z_mean) on the bias's side, the pool by the gap of the samples' means for a bias above 0.
plan: Name the candidate causes and their traces

decisions.decision: First design dropped before any run
decisions.why: the review showed its mechanism (a small pool) predicts almost no effect for the daily pick and a sign the share probe contradicted, and its 'all rows' arm changed both the pool and the information

decisions.decision: 800 worlds and a closing band of 0.08
decisions.why: at 200 worlds a mean z's 90% interval is about +-0.12 wide and could never close inside +-0.05

decisions.decision: dclab-core 0.120.1 adds the samples' mean to the holdout reading
decisions.why: the skew (the percentile midpoint against the mean) can only be read with it

findings.defect: the 'all rows' arm changed the pool and the information at once
findings.scenario: the latest interval read 1.17 (daily) and 1.29 (share) times wider than the all-rows one on 40 probe worlds
findings.cause: a larger pool is also more data
findings.fix: the all-rows arms reported only; the pool read by the gap of the samples' means

findings.defect: the gate compared z, which mixes a centre shift with a width change
findings.scenario: a wider latest interval pulls its z toward 0
findings.fix: the centres compared in value units

findings.defect: the named mechanism predicted almost no daily effect, and the share probe pointed the other way
findings.scenario: resampling bites only the maximum; a day's best of 4.4 rows from about 380 distinct rows rarely repeats; probe gap +0.11 for share where the pool predicts below 0
findings.cause: a mechanism written without checking its sign
findings.fix: the cause read by the skew first, the pool only by the sign of the samples' means' gap

findings.defect: one rule for both decisions, and 'close' by failing to reject
findings.scenario: share explained by the pool and daily not would have been dropped; a real +0.10 could be closed as chance
findings.cause: joint routing; a test that cannot reject read as proof
findings.fix: each decision its own verdict; closed only inside a band

findings.defect: tests missed the mixed cases and the share pair's realised value
findings.scenario: only the daily pair was checked
findings.fix: mixed-case verdict tests and both pairs checked

findings.defect: 'the midpoint' could still be named by failing to reject
findings.scenario: bias [0.04, 0.20] with z_mean [-0.01, 0.18] would name the skew although the mean sits where the midpoint does
findings.cause: z_mean reaching 0 is not a skew
findings.fix: a per-world skew z_mid - z_mean (the realised value cancels) must lie on the bias's side

findings.defect: the pool test had no direction and compared midpoints
findings.scenario: a bias below 0 with a gap below 0 would name the pool, which can only push the realised value above
findings.cause: no sign; the midpoints carry each arm's skew
findings.fix: the pool only for a bias above 0, the gap on the samples' means

findings.scenario: a mean z's 90% interval is about +-0.12 wide, never inside +-0.05
findings.cause: worlds too few for the band
findings.fix: 800 worlds (2000 to 2799) and a band of 0.08

findings.scenario: it called verdict twice with different inputs
findings.fix: a test feeding report() rows where only share's latest arm sits off

measurements.name: daily_centre_v1: 800 invented worlds a decision, the decision core alone, on 0d47ff0a
measurements.gate: per decision on its latest arm: the bias by the 90% interval of mean z_mid (established, closed inside 0.08, else inconclusive); the skew by mean (z_mid - z_mean) on the bias's side with mean z_mean reaching 0; the pool by the samples' means' gap below 0 for a bias above 0
measurements.result: daily: mean z_mid +0.04 (-0.02 to +0.10): inconclusive; skew -0.016 to -0.007; z_mean -0.01 to +0.12. share: mean z_mid +0.07 (+0.01 to +0.13): established; skew +0.035 to +0.047; z_mean -0.03 to +0.09: the midpoint (the samples' skew). Samples' means' gap latest minus all: daily -0.05 to +0.04, share -0.05 to +0.00. RMS z: daily 1.06, share 0.98; daily_ties_v1 had read mean z +0.10 to +0.16 on 200 worlds an arm
limits: the daily bias is not established at 800 worlds; daily_ties_v1's +0.10 to +0.16 was partly chance

outcome: The realised value's small lead over the interval's centre is the samples' skew for a share capacity (their mean sits above the percentile midpoint); the pool is ruled out; for one call a day the bias is not established. The interval's edges stand; its centre is the samples' mean.
lessons: Check a mechanism's predicted sign against a small probe before building a gate on it
Size the worlds so every outcome of the gate is reachable, closing included
A cause is named only when its own interval points the bias's way, never when another interval fails to reject
risks: Known worlds clear the core, not the replica
